newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains down, sterling strength blamed.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains down, sterling strength blamed.

text.p: LIFFE grains were again sent down by the strength of sterling, traders said.
One trader characterised the volume on wheat, which totalled 422 lots as "not too bad."
There were buyers, but in the current uncertain market, interest was limited to those with a good reason to buy, he said.

He noted that although sterling had risen through the day, wheat futures had fallen early and mostly stayed down. Active November, for example, had opened one stg lower at 82.65 stg and closed 1.15 stg lower at 82.50, its low of the day, having seen a high of 83.00 stg.
Barley also fell, with November last traded 1.00 stg lower at 79.00. November volume was 70 lots of a total 85.
Delivered grains also eased, physical market brokers said. Prices were generally around one stg down. Although they could report a list of trades, the volume behind them was limited, they said.
